sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark.

questions.q: (a) Which gas makes mercury lose its meniscus? (b) Write the formula of the compound formed.
questions.answer: (a) Ozone. (b) Mercury(I) oxide, Hg2O (sticks to glass).

questions.q: Complete and balance: (a) XeF6 + 2H2O → ______ (b) NaCl + conc. H2SO4 (423 K) → ______.
questions.answer: (a) XeOF4 + 2HF. (b) NaHSO4 + HCl.

questions.q: Fill in: (a) The catalyst in the Contact process is ______. (b) The shape of XeO3 is ______.
questions.answer: (a) V2O5. (b) trigonal pyramidal.

questions.q: State true or false: (a) SO2 acts as a reducing agent. (b) Oxygen shows an oxidation state of +6 like sulphur.
questions.answer: (a) True. (b) False – oxygen shows −2 (and −1, +2 in OF2); it has no +6 state.

questions.q: Match: (a) Tailing of mercury (b) Blue CuSO4 → white (c) Yellow crystalline solid with (i) rhombic sulphur (ii) conc. H2SO4 (iii) ozone.
Name (a) the oxidation states shown by chlorine in HClO4 and (b) the geometry of XeF2.
questions.answer: (a) +7. (b) Linear.

questions.q: Write (a) the formula of oleum and (b) the use of SO2.
questions.answer: (a) H2S2O7. (b) Bleaching of wool and silk (and making H2SO4).

questions.q: Complete: (a) Noble gases have ______ electron gain enthalpy. (b) The halogen which is liquid at room temperature is ______.
questions.answer: (a) positive. (b) bromine.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Explain why mercury loses its meniscus (tailing) in contact with ozone.
questions.answer: Ozone oxidises mercury to mercury(I) oxide (2Hg + O3 → Hg2O + O2), which dissolves in mercury and sticks to glass, so the meniscus is lost.

questions.q: Why is SO2 a reducing agent? Give a reaction.
questions.answer: In SO2 sulphur is in +4 state and can be oxidised to +6. It decolourises acidified KMnO4: 5SO2 + 2MnO4− + 2H2O → 5SO4^2− + 4H+ + 2Mn^2+.

questions.q: Write the reaction of XeF6 with water giving XeO3 and state the shape of XeO3.
questions.answer: XeF6 + 3H2O → XeO3 + 6HF. XeO3 is trigonal pyramidal with sp³ hybridisation (one lone pair).

questions.q: How does ozone act as an oxidising agent? Give an example.
questions.answer: Ozone readily gives up an oxygen atom (O3 → O2 + [O]). PbS + 4O3 → PbSO4 + 4O2; it also liberates iodine from KI.

questions.q: Why does sulphur dioxide behave as a reducing agent while sulphur trioxide does not?
questions.answer: In SO2 sulphur has the oxidation state +4 (can rise to +6); in SO3 sulphur is already in its highest state +6 and can only be reduced.

questions.q: Why are noble gases chemically inert?
questions.answer: They have completely filled valence shells (ns² np⁶), very high ionisation enthalpies and positive electron gain enthalpies.

questions.q: Write the reaction for the preparation of chlorine from HCl and MnO2.
questions.answer: MnO2 + 4HCl → MnCl2 + Cl2 + 2H2O.

questions.q: What are interhalogen compounds? Give two examples.
questions.answer: Compounds formed between two different halogens, e.g. ClF3 and IF7.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Describe the manufacture of sulphuric acid by the Contact process with the reactions.
questions.answer: Steps: S + O2 → SO2; SO2 is purified and oxidised: 2SO2 + O2 ⇌ 2SO3 over V2O5 at 673–723 K and 2 bar; SO3 is absorbed in conc. H2SO4 to give oleum (SO3 + H2SO4 → H2S2O7) and diluted with water: H2S2O7 + H2O → 2H2SO4.

questions.q: Explain the oxidising and dehydrating properties of concentrated sulphuric acid with examples.
questions.answer: Oxidising: Cu + 2H2SO4 → CuSO4 + SO2 + 2H2O; C + 2H2SO4 → CO2 + 2SO2 + 2H2O. Dehydrating: it removes water from blue vitriol (CuSO4·5H2O → white CuSO4) and chars sugar (C12H22O11 → 12C + 11H2O).

questions.q: Write the preparation, structure and reaction with water of XeF6.
questions.answer: Xe + 3F2 → XeF6 at 573 K and 60–70 atm. Structure: distorted octahedral (sp³d³). Hydrolysis: XeF6 + 3H2O → XeO3 + 6HF, partial hydrolysis gives XeOF4.

questions.q: Compare the oxidising power and oxidation states of the halogens.
questions.answer: Oxidising power decreases F2 > Cl2 > Br2 > I2 (F2 displaces the others from their halides). Fluorine shows only −1; Cl, Br and I show −1, +1, +3, +5 and +7 in oxoacids and interhalogens.

questions.q: Explain the ozone layer depletion and its harmful effects.
questions.answer: Ozone in the stratosphere absorbs harmful UV radiation. CFCs release Cl atoms which convert O3 into O2 in a chain reaction (Cl + O3 → ClO + O2). The thinning of the layer causes skin cancer, cataracts and damage to crops and plankton.

questions.q: How is hydrogen chloride prepared in the laboratory? Why is it called a strong acid?
questions.answer: NaCl + H2SO4 (conc.) → NaHSO4 + HCl at 420 K (and at higher temperature Na2SO4). In water it ionises completely: HCl + H2O → H3O+ + Cl−, hence a strong acid.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: (a) Explain SO2 as a reducing agent with two reactions. (b) Describe the preparation of XeO3 and its structure.
questions.answer:
(a) 5SO2 + 2KMnO4 + 2H2O → K2SO4 + 2MnSO4 + 2H2SO4 (purple colour discharged); SO2 + 2Fe^3+ + 2H2O → SO4^2− + 4H+ + 2Fe^2+. Sulphur is oxidised from +4 to +6.
(b) XeF6 + 3H2O → XeO3 + 6HF; XeO3 is a colourless explosive solid, trigonal pyramidal (sp³ with one lone pair).

questions.q: (a) Give the preparation of ozone and write two reactions showing its oxidising property. (b) State two uses of ozone.
questions.answer:
(a) Silent electric discharge through dry oxygen: 3O2 → 2O3. Oxidising reactions: PbS + 4O3 → PbSO4 + 4O2; 2KI + H2O + O3 → 2KOH + I2 + O2; it also converts Hg to Hg2O (tailing).
(b) Sterilisation of drinking water and bleaching of oils and waxes.

questions.q: (a) Compare the properties of F, Cl, Br and I in oxidising power, bond enthalpy and electronegativity. (b) Write the oxoacids of chlorine in increasing order of acidic strength with reasons.
questions.answer:
(a) Electronegativity and oxidising power decrease from F to I; the bond enthalpy of Cl–Cl (243 kJ mol^-1) exceeds that of F–F (158) due to lone-pair repulsion in the small F2 and then decreases to I2 (151).
(b) HOCl < HClO2 < HClO3 < HClO4: increasing oxidation state of Cl and number of oxygens stabilise the anion by resonance.

questions.q: (a) Describe the xenon fluorides with conditions of preparation and shapes. (b) Write the hydrolysis of XeF4 and XeF6. (c) State two uses of noble gases.
questions.answer:
(a) XeF2 (Xe : F2 = 2 : 1, 673 K) linear; XeF4 (1 : 5, 873 K, 7 bar) square planar; XeF6 (1 : 20, 573 K, 60–70 bar) distorted octahedral.
(b) 6XeF4 + 12H2O → 4Xe + 2XeO3 + 24HF + 3O2; XeF6 + 3H2O → XeO3 + 6HF.
(c) He is used in balloons and for diving (with oxygen); Ar for an inert atmosphere in welding and in electric bulbs.
